requirements.text: The game is a fast-paced 2D side-scrolling brawler.
The game is built with the Phaser engine (Arcade physics, sprite animation, input).
The player controls a single hero character, Zed.
The player can move left and right (A/D or Left/Right arrows).
The player can jump (W or Space; alternate Up arrow).
Sprite animations exist for player idle, walk and jump.
Light attack is bound to J (alternate Z).
Heavy attack is bound to K (alternate X).
Dodge is bound to L (alternate C).
Pick up is bound to P (alternate N).
Parry is bound to T (alternate M).
Block is bound to I (alternate V).
The player has light and heavy attacks that deliver punchy hits.
Light and heavy attacks chain into combos through one attack state machine with cancel windows and hit stun.
Offence includes combo and juggle routes.
The player has defensive tools: block, dodge and parry.
The player can pick up objects and use them in combat.
Hits provide hit-stop and feedback so telegraphs and impacts read clearly.
Health, damage values and hitbox/hurtbox data are shared in one place that every system reads.
Hits register damage and the player can die when health reaches zero.
Tier 0 ships one enemy type.
Enemies chase the player and attack.
An attacker cap limits how many enemies attack the player at once.
Rust Grunt (The Iron Line) has a Rust Jab Combo: a quick 1-2-3 punch string, light damage, used to interrupt the player.
Rust Grunt has a Helmet Headbutt: short windup forward lunge that causes brief stun, used when the player is too close or grabs too often.
Rust Bruiser has a downward smash with medium startup that causes ground bounce and breaks the player's block.
Rust Bruiser has a Rust Uppercut that launches the player, usable as anti-air against frequent jumping.
Rust Bruiser has a Body Check: short dash with super armour that knocks the player back and can interrupt combos.
Rust Ranger has a ranged Taser Shot that does light damage and brief stun.
Rust Ranger has a Baton Strike with very quick startup that interrupts player combos at close range.
Rust Specialist (Copper Fang) has Fang Jab (very fast, brief stun), Copper Cross (medium damage, stagger, used after dodging) and Shield Bash (pushes back, breaks guard).
There are five Rust unit types: Grunts, Bruisers, Rangers, Specialists, Overseers (bosses).
There are five Overseer bosses: Kade Voss, Rhea Calder, Silas Wren, Dr. Maren Holt, Halden Varr, each with a distinct arena and two phases.
Kade Voss phase 2 triggers at 50% HP.
Rhea Calder phase 2 triggers at 40% HP.
Silas Wren phase 2 triggers at 50% HP.
Dr. Maren Holt phase 2 triggers at 40% HP.
Halden Varr phase 2 triggers at 30% HP.
Voss Predictive Strike telegraphs a red line, then fires a laser along it after 1 second.
Voss Predictive Lockdown disables the player's special meter for 10 seconds.
Voss Drone Swarm summons 3-5 destroyable orbiting drones.
Calder Furnace Slam creates molten cracks that explode after 2 seconds.
Enemies spawn in waves.
The wave spawner defines spawn triggers, rate, cap and positions.
Difficulty comes from how waves arrive.
Core loop: enter city level, enemies spawn, fight, wave cleared, reach the end, level won, next level begins.
The player wins by clearing the wave/arena (fighting to the end of the level past Rust enemies) within the time frame.
The player loses when the health bar reaches zero.
The player loses when the timer runs out.
A timer tracks the level time limit.
After a lose state or time-out the player can retry.
The arena camera locks during the fight.
World bounds keep the player and enemies inside the arena.
An unreachable-enemy failsafe prevents a soft lock when an enemy is off-screen.
The HUD shows player health and the timer.
Win and lose screens show the player why they won or lost.
The main menu has four options in order: Fight, Controls, Options, Quit.
The Fight menu option starts the game.
Menu title reads THE REBELLION in heavy condensed cream type on a black strip tilted about 2 degrees, with subtitle Fists of the Fallen City in mustard monospace.
Each menu option is a separate torn-edge paper strip, tilted slightly; Fight is mustard, Controls cream, Options forest green, Quit warm brown.
The selected menu option straightens, moves right (about 10px in about 100 ms), shows a leading '>' marker and takes the brightest colour; mouse hover gives the same feedback.
Menu navigation uses W/S to select and Enter to confirm, with mouse click matching; footer hint 'W/S select / Enter confirm' sits bottom right.
The Controls screen lists the action-to-key table (move, jump, light, heavy, dodge, pick up, parry, block).
Options menu has a Music volume slider that changes game music level.
Options menu has an SFX volume slider covering hits, parries and dodges.
Options menu has a Fullscreen setting that makes the game screen fullscreen.
The menu scene shows a brick wall with posters on the left half and a dusk city street on the right.
The menu background uses three parallax layers: sky and sun, far and near buildings, brick wall foreground.
Two non-interactive background posters appear: 'Local Heroes Benefit: Keep the Lights On' and Rust Notice 114 'CURFEW' struck through.
The title screen shows a THE REBELLION stencil banner on a mustard halftone poster, 'FISTS OF THE FALLEN CITY' in huge block type with a crack, and a raised-fist stamp.
The title screen shows a fallen-skyline dusk city with lit windows, one toppled tower, drifting smoke and sweeping searchlights.
The title screen shows pasted text 'HOLD THE LINE', 'Nobody's coming. Be somebody.', a 'Rebels' spray tag, 'Sector 7 ->' and 'we were here'.
The title screen shows a blinking 'PRESS ANY BUTTON' prompt in a pill on hazard tape at the bottom.
Click, any key or a gamepad button on the title screen starts a short 'Loading the fallen city' bar, then it resets.
The palette is mustard #E1A92B, brick red #9C3B2E/#7A2F25, forest green #2F5D3A, warm brown #6B4A2F, cream #E8DCC0, near-black #1D1A16.
Menu visual style uses flat shapes with torn uneven edges, no gradients or glow; heavy condensed display type and monospace small print.
Atmosphere is lived-in, human, culturally rich, hopeful and energetic (corner shops, murals, basketball courts, food stalls, community gardens).
Zed's outfit carries mustard yellow, brick red and forest green.
Tier 0 scope is one character, one enemy type, waves and a timer.
The story is that Zed fights to take Fallen City back from Rust, one district at a time, and to find his missing father.

ambiguities.why: GDD requires a time frame and a timer-out lose state but gives no duration.

ambiguities.topic: Player health and all damage values
ambiguities.why: Only qualitative values (light, medium, high); no numeric HP or damage for player or enemies.

ambiguities.topic: Wave counts, sizes, rate, attacker cap number
ambiguities.why: Spawn rate, cap and wave composition are named but undefined.

ambiguities.topic: Which enemy type is the Tier 0 enemy
ambiguities.why: One enemy type first, but not named; Rust Grunt is the likely candidate (inferred only).
Combo strings, cancel windows, hit stun frames and juggle routes are not specified for the player.
Only keys and existence stated; no windows, costs or effects. Special meter is referenced (Voss disables it) but never defined.
All three primary docx files contain embedded images (menu mockup, title screen art, Rebellion diagrams); pixel content is not in requirements.

ambiguities.topic: Level and district count, level order, next-level progression
ambiguities.why: Core loop mentions next level begins but number of levels, arenas and which tier includes bosses is not stated.
GDD gives no tier for Bruisers, Rangers, Specialists or Overseers; left null.
Win/lose screens are required but no pause menu, retry button layout or lose-screen content is described.
Controls strip is cream and a key table exists, but whether it is a separate screen or rebindable is not stated. The Options table says SFX 'on or off' while the function column says slider.

ambiguities.topic: Menu Fight vs Title screen flow
ambiguities.why: Title screen 'loading bar then it resets' is unclear about whether it proceeds to the main menu.
Text such as 'Face Paced', 'Desponds On', and the duplicated Wave Spawner role (same text as Game State Agent) suggest copy errors; Wave Spawner role is taken from the Technical Strategy table.
